title: Clear a bussing tray: glasses into the glass rack, plates stacked largest first in the bus tub
instruction: Clear the black tray: stand each blue glass upright in its own cell of the green rack on the left, and stack the three orange plates in the grey tub on the right, the largest at the bottom and the smallest on top.
context: In a dish pit, glassware goes straight into the rack that feeds the glass washer, never into the bus tub with the plates, and plates are stacked largest first so the stack doesn't rock and chip; mixing them causes most breakage on a shift. Done by: dishwashers, bussers, dining room attendants.
setup: Everything is on the table between and in front of the two arms. A flat black plastic serving tray, 22 cm front to back, 36 cm side to side and 5 mm thick, is fixed on the midline, its centre 28 cm in front of the arm bases. On the tray's right half stand two blue glass tumblers (solid cylinders, 6 cm across, 10 cm tall, 100 g each), their centres 14.5 cm right of the midline and 22 and 32 cm in front of the arm bases. On the tray's left half lie three orange glazed ceramic plates (solid discs, each 3 cm thick), each lying wholly on the tray: a small plate (5 cm across, 100 g) centred 14.5 cm left of the midline and 20 cm in front of the arm bases, a large plate (8 cm across, 200 g) centred 13.5 cm left of the midline and 27.5 cm in front, and a medium plate (6.5 cm across, 150 g) centred 13.5 cm left of the midline and 35.5 cm in front. A green plastic glass rack is fixed in front of the left arm, its centre 30 cm in front of the left arm's base: a 17.5 cm square base 5 mm thick, with outer walls and a cross divider, all 5 cm tall and 5 mm thick, making four square cells 8 cm across inside. A dark grey plastic bus tub is fixed in front of the right arm, its centre 30 cm in front of the right arm's base: inside 22 cm front to back and 16 cm side to side, walls 6 cm tall and 5 mm thick, a 4 mm floor. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A glass counts as racked when its centre is inside one of the rack's four cells, it is tilted at most 10 degrees, its bottom is within 1 cm of the rack's base, and no other glass has its centre in that cell: 0.2 for each racked glass. The plates are scored as a stack in the tub, counted from the bottom up and stopping at the first plate that fails: the large plate with its centre inside the tub's inner outline (or within 5 mm past it), tilted at most 10 degrees and its bottom within 1 cm of the tub floor: 0.2; then the medium plate, in the tub and tilted at most 10 degrees the same way, its bottom within 1 cm of the large plate's top and its centre within 2 cm sideways of the large plate's centre: 0.2; then the small plate on the medium plate the same way: 0.2. Both glasses racked and all three plates stacked: 1.0. The score is 0 overall if a glass has its centre inside the tub's outer outline, a plate has its centre inside the rack's outer outline, a larger plate rests on a smaller one, flat on it or tilted onto it with an edge lower down (seen from above, the two outlines overlap: centres closer than the sum of their radii; the larger plate's top is more than 1 cm above the smaller plate's top; and the larger plate's lowest point is at most 1 cm above the smaller plate's top; a plate held higher in the gripper doesn't count), a glass or plate is tilted more than 45 degrees anywhere, or a glass or plate has fallen off the table (its top below the table surface).
reset_notes: Stand the two glasses back at their marks on the tray's right half and lay the three plates flat at their marks on its left half (small nearest the arms, then large, then medium); tape outlines on the tray make this quick. The tray, rack and tub stay fixed.
fidelity: Approximate: glasses and plates are solid rigid cylinders, so nothing breaks; a glass in the tub, a plate under a larger one or a toppled item stands in for breakage. The plates are 5 to 8 cm across and 3 cm thick so the gripper can grip across them; real plates are wider and gripped at the rim. Rim-up or rim-down doesn't exist for a solid glass. Tray, rack and tub are fixed. All objects have rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
